text:
mike: Quick follow-up from the compaction RFC. Canary shows small-batch tail spikes when compactor runs.

tara: saw this in staging too. compactor walk seems to steal CPU and triggers a pagefault spike.

josh: got a repro? is this due to memcpy remaps + global slab lock?

mike: repro: steady 6-8 concurrent requests, short sequences. When compaction runs we see ~40-80ms pauses. Logs:
```
[compactor] walk shard=2; candidates=900
[alloc] stall: waiting for staging slots; active_batches=6
[pfault] spike: 100/s -> 780/s
[compactor] finish; reclaimed=12MB
```

sophia: that pfault spike suggests we're tearing mappings. current flow is allocate dest slab -> memcpy -> update mapping -> free old under arena lock.

tara: global lock is bad for latency-sensitive tiny batches. propose incremental micro-moves and cooperative yielding.

eva: plus tenant-aware avoidance: don't touch slabs for tenants in high-SLO windows.

josh: need hotset estimator to make tenant-aware decisions. reuse kvcache sampling to score slabs.

mike: sketch: background_compactor tick (200ms), prioritized queue of slab tuples (tenant, slab, score), do up to M slabs/tick and K pages/move per slab. On publish do atomic pointer swap and free old pages after GPU-fence epoch.

sophia: pointer-swap requires epoch/RC for in-flight GPU descriptors. tie free to fence observed by kernels.

tara: add exponential backoff and token-bucket budget so compaction throttles when p99 rises.

josh: watch global fragmentation: avoiding some tenants can shift cost to others. value function: reclaimed_bytes - (pf_cost + latency_penalty). Only compact when net benefit > 0.

eva: console knobs: compaction.mode={aggressive,balanced,conservative}, compaction.slo_avoidance=true/false, and tenant.meta.compact_priority.

mike: plan: prototype 2w, canary 1m. infra-bot: add feature flag ff/compactor_incremental.

infra-bot: feature flag created: ff/compactor_incremental

mike: I'll open a follow-up RFC with micro-move API, policy, and tests (including publish-failure and GPU-epoch stress).

tara: :thumbsup:
